To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spatial resolution of photo and/or thermoacoustic tomographic imaging is not limited by the finite size of the detector but by the finite bandwidth of ultrasound detectors and the limited number of detectors used in the experiment.

the spatial resolution of photoacoustic imaging with an approximate point detector is limited by the size of the point source (the photoacoustic source), the size of the detector and the bandwidth of the detector.

the spatial resolution of photoacoustic tomographic imaging can be significantly improved using the following strategies: (i) use a detector with a smaller size; (ii) use a detector that is sensitive to higher ultrasound frequencies; and (iii) increase the number of detectors used in the tomographic imaging process.

the detector size is the main limiting factor, while the detector bandwidth is of secondary importance.

the resolution of photoacoustic tomographic imaging systems with point detectors is limited by the bandwidth of the detection system, while in systems with line detectors, the resolution is limited by the size of the line detectors.
